instruction.text: Complete the sentences about the impacts of earthquakes.

atoms.sound: This destruction increases with the size of the earthquake.

atoms.a: They can cause buildings, roads and bridges to ...
atoms.sound: They can cause buildings, roads and bridges to fall down or crack.

atoms.a: Earthquakes also put human and animal lives at ...
atoms.sound: Earthquakes also put human and animal lives at risk, and sometimes cause deaths.

instruction.text: Which three natural disasters do you think earthquakes can trigger?
You’re talking to a scientist about how earthquakes trigger these natural disasters. Fill in the gaps.

hint.text: Scientists who study earthquakes and tsunamis are called seismologists.
hint.label: Did you know?

atoms.b: How does an earthquake trigger a volcanic eruption?
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '-0.5st'>How does an earthquake trigger a volcanic eruption?</prosody>

atoms.b: Earthquakes ((++shake melt)) the ground, which increases the amount of pressure in the magma storage area of the ((river ++volcano)) and can cause eruptions.

atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '-0.5st'>Why do earthquakes trigger tsunamis?</prosody>

atoms.b: When an earthquake happens under the ((++ocean moon)), energy is released into the water, and large ((++waves hurricanes)) form. This is called a tsunami.
When the ground shakes during an earthquake, ((++mountain tree)) slopes and cliffs can become unstable. Large amounts of ((++rock pop)) and soil can then collapse.

instruction.text: Do you think we have earthquakes in the UK?

hint.text: There are thousands of earthquakes across the world each day. Most of them are just so weak that they cannot be felt.

feedback.finish: The UK isn’t on a plate boundary, but we still get some small earthquakes from cracks in the plate we sit on. Our earthquakes are usually so weak that we can barely feel them.
